hypotheses.rationale: The agent used 356,500 km as the Moon’s minimum perigee distance without verification. Wikipedia’s Moon page lists the minimum perigee near 356,400 km (often 356,375–356,400 km). Using 356,500 km slightly inflates the time and leads to rounding up to 17000 hours. With the correct minimum perigee, the computed time would round to 16000 hours, changing the final thousand-hour result. This earliest incorrect input distance propagates to all later steps.
